html:
Black pepper is the dried fruit of a climbing vine native to the Western Ghats of south India, and for most of history the most traded spice in the world.

Its homeland was the Malabar coast, where rulers such as the Cheras grew rich from it. Riding the monsoon winds, Roman ships sailed to Muziris each year to buy pepper with gold. Roman cooks used it in most recipes of the Apicius cookbook.

In the Middle Ages it reached Europe through Arab traders, Alexandria and Venice. The wish to buy it at the source sent Vasco da Gama to Calicut in 1498. The Portuguese, then the Dutch East India Company, fought to control the trade, by then also grown in Sumatra and Java, where ports such as Banten lived on it. In Indian cooking, the arrival of chilli from the Americas took over much of its role.
sum: Black pepper is the dried fruit of a climbing vine native to the Western Ghats of south India, and for most of history the most traded spice in the world.
